subject: website
name: Ledger Wallet
summary: Ledger's desktop app for its hardware wallets, built unmodified from its open source (MIT) at a pinned commit. It is not Level 3: on every start it fetches feature flags from Google's Firebase Remote Config and registers an installation with Firebase, remote configuration nobody is asked about, and it decides what appears, Live Apps included. It would not be Level 4 either: balances, fees, prices and broadcast come from Ledger's servers. Keys stay on the Ledger device. Orivon refuses its analytics and error reporting. Not private: Ledger and Google see your IP address.

operations.name: Keep accounts and settings on this computer
operations.note: Files in this app's own folder, with no Ledger account. An optional password encrypts them. Nothing is sent by this step.

operations.name: Show and verify a receive address
operations.note: The Ledger device derives the address from the seed it holds and shows it on its own screen, where the person checks it.

operations.name: Send: sign a transaction on the device
operations.note: Signed and confirmed on the device. Nonces, unspent outputs and fees come from Ledger's servers, which can mislead or refuse to relay; what the device shows and the person confirms is what is signed.

operations.name: Read balances, history, fees and prices
operations.note: A passive read from Ledger's servers and the explorers and price sources they relay, with nothing to check the answer against.

operations.name: Install device apps and update firmware
operations.note: The code does what it promises, but Ledger's servers script the steps over a secure channel to the device, so Ledger decides what is installed.

operations.name: Swap, buy, sell and earn in Live Apps
operations.note: Each is a partner's web app served remotely and opened from the app's menus; a dapp from Discover first shows a notice that Ledger does not run it. Its code cannot be checked here.

connections.name: Feature flags (Google Firebase Remote Config and Installations)
connections.note: Fetched on every start and polled, with no question asked. Decides which features and Live Apps appear, and gives Google an installation id and your IP address.

connections.name: Ledger's blockchain servers (coin.ledger.com, explorers, proxies)
connections.note: Balances, history, fees and broadcast for each coin you add, answered by Ledger or the explorers it relays, unchecked. Each sees the addresses you add and your IP address.

connections.name: Prices, token data and images (Ledger and other hosts)
connections.note: Change displayed values, token lists and icons only. Each host sees your IP address.

connections.name: Live App catalogue and partner apps (swap, earn, buy)
connections.note: The catalogue is read from Ledger; each partner app loads from its own server only when you open it.

connections.name: Device and account services (manager, gateway, script runner, Ledger Sync)
connections.note: App and firmware lists, the secure channel that checks and updates the device, and Ledger Sync once you turn it on. Ledger learns your device model and apps.
